title: Chicken Teriyaki Rice Bowls
subtitle: seared chicken thighs in a glossy homemade teriyaki, over jasmine rice with broccoli & carrots
imageAlt: Sliced glossy teriyaki chicken over white rice with broccoli and carrots in a cream bowl
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

breakdown: Rice vinegar, garlic, ginger, cornstarch, oil, sesame seeds

beforeYouStart.text: Frozen thighs? Thaw in the fridge overnight (about 24 h for 1 kg).
Start the rice first — it needs 15 minutes plus a 10 minute rest.
Whisk the teriyaki sauce before you start cooking; the pan part goes fast.

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Bring it to a boil with the water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on. Fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Mix the teriyaki
steps.text: In a jug, whisk the soy sauce, water, honey, brown sugar, rice vinegar, garlic and ginger. Keep the cornstarch slurry separate.

steps.title: Steam the veg
steps.text: Put the broccoli and carrots in a pot with 2 cm of water, cover and steam over medium-high 4–5 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain and toss with the butter and a pinch of salt.

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.text: Pat the thighs dry and season with salt, pepper and garlic powder. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Sear smooth side down 5–6 minutes until deep golden, flip and cook 4–5 minutes more, until 74°C (165°F) inside.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium. Pour the sauce around the chicken and simmer 2 minutes, then stir in the cornstarch slurry and simmer 1 minute more, turning the chicken, until the sauce is glossy and coats a spoon.

steps.title: Slice and build the bowls
steps.text: Rest the chicken 3 minutes, then slice. Fill bowls with rice, veg and chicken, spoon over extra sauce from the pan and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

fixIt.fix: Simmer 1–2 minutes longer — it thickens as it bubbles and again as it cools.
Heat was too high once the sugar went in. Add 2–3 tbsp water off the heat and stir to loosen.
Use low-sodium soy next time; for now add a splash of water and a little more honey.
Pan wasn't hot enough or the chicken was wet. Pat dry, and don't move it for the first 5 minutes.

saleTip: Boneless thighs drop to about $9–11/kg in No Frills club-pack flyer weeks — buy 2 kg and freeze half in a flat bag.
swap: Chicken breast works (sear 4–5 min a side to 74°C / 165°F). Salmon also loves this sauce — 4 fillets, 4 min a side.
leftovers: Pack in containers with the sauce: rice, veg, chicken. Fridge 3–4 days.
source: Based on tested homemade teriyaki methods (RecipeTin Eats, Just One Cookbook): soy + sweetener + vinegar reduced with a cornstarch slurry; safe temp per Health Canada.
prepAhead: Mix the teriyaki sauce (without the slurry) up to 5 days ahead; keep in a jar in the fridge.
Cut the broccoli and slice the carrots a day ahead.
Cook the rice the day before for meal-prep bowls.
reheat: Microwave the bowl covered with a splash of water, 2–3 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming (74°C / 165°F).

basic.note: Seared chicken with a 4-ingredient teriyaki over rice and steamed broccoli.

stepNotes.1: Basic: soy sauce, water, honey, brown sugar and garlic.
stepNotes.2: Basic: broccoli only, a pinch of salt.

fancy.note: Sticky glazed thighs sliced over rice with honey-glazed carrots, toasted sesame and a soft-boiled egg.

stepNotes.2: Fancy: toss the veg with the sesame oil.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Soft-boil the eggs 6½ minutes, cool in cold water and halve. Build each bowl in sections — rice, broccoli, carrots, sliced chicken — with half an egg on top, extra glaze and sesame seeds.

plating: Arrange each topping in its own section of the bowl.
Fan the sliced chicken; spoon glaze only over the chicken.
Half a soft egg, yolk up, then sesame seeds.

why.1-7: The slurry turns the thin sauce into a sticky glaze.
why.1-4: Rice vinegar balances the sweetness. Skip it and the glaze is sweeter.
why.1-6: Ginger adds warmth. Without it the teriyaki is simpler but still good.

funFact: Teriyaki means “glossy grilling” in Japanese: teri is the shine of the sweet soy glaze and yaki means grilled.
